title: Gemcitabine and docetaxel for soft tissue sarcoma
indication: Locally advanced unresectable or metastatic soft tissue sarcoma
purpose: The treatment aims to control advanced sarcoma and help cancer-related symptoms. The choice depends on sarcoma subtype, previous treatment, fitness and your priorities; your consultant explains why this combination is being considered.
schedule: NCCP 00501 gives gemcitabine 675 mg/m² on days 1 and 8, with docetaxel 75 mg/m² on day 8. Repeat every 21 days for up to 6 cycles if suitable. Day 8 has its own safety review and can be delayed or omitted on clinical advice.
admin: Gemcitabine is infused over 90 minutes on both days 1 and 8. On day 8 it is followed by docetaxel over 60 minutes. Allow additional time for blood tests, review, line care and observation.
scope: This is the gemcitabine 675 mg/m², 90-minute sarcoma schedule. It must not be replaced by a 1000 mg/m² or 30-minute gemcitabine schedule from another regimen. The sarcoma use described by this source is off-label and requires a documented discussion and consent under local policy.
consent: Discuss the treatment goal, alternatives including supportive care, uncertainty of benefit, common and serious risks, lasting effects and individual priorities. Record questions and the agreed plan. This is the gemcitabine 675 mg/m², 90-minute sarcoma schedule. It must not be replaced by a 1000 mg/m² or 30-minute gemcitabine schedule from another regimen. The sarcoma use described by this source is off-label and requires a documented discussion and consent under local policy.
generic: Discuss low blood counts with serious infection or sepsis, anaemia and bleeding; nausea or vomiting; mouth soreness, appetite or taste change, diarrhoea or constipation; tiredness, hair and skin changes; infusion reactions and intravenous-line complications; fertility, pregnancy and breastfeeding effects; and the possibility of lasting organ injury, rare later cancers or death from serious treatment complications. Risks differ between medicines and people. The medicine-specific section explains the main additional risks for this regimen.

agents.name: Gemcitabine
agents.explanation: Gemcitabine interferes with making DNA, which dividing cancer cells need. Healthy blood-forming cells and other tissues can also be affected.
agents.watch: Report fever, breathlessness, new widespread rash, rapid swelling, reduced urine, unusual bruising or severe headache with visual change or confusion urgently.
risks: Low blood counts, serious infection, anaemia and bleeding
Nausea, fatigue, flu-like symptoms, mouth soreness, rash and swelling
Liver-test changes; occasionally serious liver injury
Rare serious lung inflammation, fluid leakage from blood vessels or kidney injury with breakdown of red cells
Rare severe skin reactions or a brain syndrome causing headache, seizures or visual changes; fertility and pregnancy harm

agents.name: Docetaxel
agents.explanation: Docetaxel stabilises tiny structures called microtubules. Cells need these to separate their chromosomes during division; disrupting the process can stop cancer cells multiplying. Healthy dividing cells are also affected.
agents.watch: Take the prescribed dexamethasone before docetaxel. Report fever, severe abdominal pain or diarrhoea, breathlessness, swelling, persistent numbness or new blurred vision promptly. Tell staff immediately about any infusion reaction.
risks: Low blood counts, infection or sepsis; severe bowel inflammation may occur with or without low white cells
Hair loss, which can sometimes persist; mouth soreness, fatigue and nail changes
Numbness, tingling or weakness from nerve injury, sometimes lasting
Fluid retention, swelling and allergic infusion reactions despite premedication
Rare severe skin reactions, lung inflammation or sight-threatening eye effects; fertility and pregnancy harm

support.title: Preparation and support medicines
support.text: Get the day 7–9 dexamethasone prescription before the day 8 visit. Contact the team if doses were missed or vomited; do not silently double doses. Review diabetes control, infection symptoms and all medicines. Reconcile steroid premedication with any anti-sickness steroids. Take dexamethasone 8 mg by mouth twice daily for 3 days, starting day 7, unless your team prescribes an explicitly revised plan; NCCP requires at least 3 doses before docetaxel. This reduces allergic reactions and fluid retention. Both drugs have low emetogenic classification in this source. G-CSF may be used based on the prescribed risk plan; it is not mandatory for every patient in NCCP 00501.

support.title: Access and practical care
support.text: The team chooses suitable intravenous access and explains line care. Tell the nurse immediately about burning, pain, redness or swelling during an injection or drip. Do not wait for the visit to finish. If you have a port or PICC, agree dressing, flushing and removal arrangements.

support.title: Fertility and pregnancy precautions
support.text: Discuss fertility preservation before treatment. Avoid pregnancy and breastfeeding as directed. Your team must give written contraception and post-treatment precautions for every medicine, using current product information; the required duration may differ by medicine and between patients.

support.title: Your wider treatment plan
support.text: A sarcoma multidisciplinary team reviews the exact pathology, disease extent, prior treatment, fitness and your priorities. Surgery and radiotherapy may help local control in selected circumstances; their role and timing are decided separately. Chemotherapy does not automatically replace an operation or radiotherapy. Supportive and palliative care can be used alongside cancer treatment to help symptoms and daily life.

monitoring.title: Tests and care through treatment

rows.label: Safety tests and symptoms
cells: Complete baseline checks in the full treatment reference.
Repeat cycle tests and the regimen-specific checks in your written test plan.
Report symptoms promptly; extra tests may be needed.
Follow abnormal results and lasting effects until a plan is agreed.

rows.label: Medicines and practical care
cells: Confirm the written treatment and support prescriptions.
Record actual treatment, support and any safety hold.
Follow the support and contact plan.
Review ongoing support and line-care or removal needs.

rows.label: Cancer treatment and follow-up
cells: Agree the treatment goal and baseline cancer assessment.
Review benefit using the specialist plan.
Report new or changing cancer-related symptoms.
Agree the next sarcoma treatment or follow-up plan.

monitoring.note: Safety testing and cancer-response assessment have different purposes. Your plan may change after illness or a dose adjustment.

tests.label: Full blood count
tests.purpose: Check white cells for infection risk, haemoglobin for anaemia and platelets for bleeding risk.
tests.timing: At baseline and before the day 1 and day 8 treatment decisions. Day 1 and day 8 count thresholds differ.

tests.label: Kidney and liver tests
tests.purpose: Check safe medicine handling and identify kidney or liver effects.
tests.timing: At baseline and before each cycle; repeat sooner for symptoms, abnormal results or clinical concerns.

tests.label: Bone profile
tests.timing: Before treatment; repeat later only if clinically indicated.

tests.label: Medicines and symptoms
tests.purpose: Check interactions, treatment toxicity and whether support prescriptions are complete.
tests.timing: Before treatment and at each treatment review; report new symptoms or medicine changes between visits.

tests.label: Cancer response and follow-up
tests.purpose: Assess cancer control separately from safety blood tests.
tests.timing: Your consultant sets the scan and clinical-review schedule according to the sarcoma and treatment aim.

evidence.title: GeDDiS: gemcitabine/docetaxel versus doxorubicin
evidence.summary: GeDDiS tested these gemcitabine/docetaxel doses and infusion durations against doxorubicin 75 mg/m² in previously untreated advanced soft tissue sarcoma. The combination did not improve progression-free or overall survival and was harder to deliver. The study did not show a clear superior effect in a particular histological subgroup.
evidence.intro: GeDDiS tested these gemcitabine/docetaxel doses and infusion durations against doxorubicin 75 mg/m² in previously untreated advanced soft tissue sarcoma. The combination did not improve progression-free or overall survival and was harder to deliver. The study did not show a clear superior effect in a particular histological subgroup.
evidence.caveat: A first-line comparison does not establish the best later-line choice for every sarcoma subtype. Individual suitability and prior treatment matter. Do not import growth-factor schedules or supportive orders from the trial into the NCCP regimen automatically.
